Most of your specific examples are valid, but I'd like to point out that while conventional medicine is great at what it knows how to do, there are a few areas where it falls short - for example areas such as chronic illnesses and preventative medicine.

Conventional medicine is great at treating acute and severe conditions, delivering babies and so on, but when it comes to treating long term fatigue, a weak immune system, chronic neuropathic pain, depression, or other such conditions, it has a nasty habit of brushing off the disease as psychosomatic, doing a surgery that eventually just makes things worse, or simply prescribing narcotics for the rest of the patient's life. These cases are where a holistic approach is necessary, so alternative medicine can be much more useful. While conventional medicine is great at focusing on a single area and breaking it down further and further to find something to target with surgical blades or powerful drugs, it isn't so good at looking at the whole picture and considering the individual's health from multiple angles at once.

I'll put aside the issue of drug overprescription and the pharmaceutical industry's influence on so many doctors without any integrity; in any health industry there are good practitioners and bad practitioners. Likewise, there are plenty of alternative medicine practitioners using invented modalities that simply don't work (eg. crystals, reiki, homeopathy etc) and are just there to cash in on people whose minds are so open their brains are falling out. Again, good practitioners and bad practitioners are present in every health industry. My point is that there's a time and a place for the alternative medicines that actually work, and when used correctly they can be very helpful. This works both ways, though.

There's also a time and a place for conventional medicine, too, and good alternative practitioners understand this and encourage their patients to keep in touch with their doctor as well, and refer their patient to their GP they can't help them. Most doctors unfortunately haven't reached the point of referring patients on to alternative practitioners when the patient's condition can't really be treated with conventional medicine yet; instead they just throw drugs and surgery at the problem.

When your whole system of medicine is based on focusing on the individual and their constitution to make an accurate and personalized prescription, it becomes nonsensical to use a research method where you give a large sample of patients with similar symptoms the same treatment. Randomized controlled trials are considered the gold standard of medical research, and anything less is always brushed off as "not good enough" or "unconvincing evidence".
